### FRESNO STATE OVER 6.5 WINS (-120)

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Youmans builds the case on Matt Entz, who won two FCS national titles at North Dakota State on a 60-11 record and then turned a losing Fresno State team into a 9-4 finish in his first year. He judges that team to have been held back by mediocre quarterback play and notes Entz answered it with Maryland transfer Khristian Martin, a dual-threat. Four of the top five pass catchers return, Josiah Freeman among them, and three of the Pac-12's better offensive linemen block for experienced backs Bryson Donelson and Rayshon Luke. He flags the Oct. 10 home game with Boise State as possibly the most important matchup of Pac-12 play, recalling that Entz's Fresno side won 30-7 at Boise as a 17-point underdog. After a September trip to USC he sees a realistic run of three straight wins over Sacramento State, San Jose State and Rice, and notes Circa posted 6.5 with the league's 12th flex game included.

*Rests on:* coaching (Entz year two); quarterback (Khristian Martin); returning receivers and offensive line; schedule

**The argument — TTW reference notes**

Youmans argues the Big Ten is loaded again — he names Ohio State, Oregon and Indiana — while Michigan has been losing ground. He traces the fallout from the Harbaugh era to the firing of Sherrone Moore, whose staff he calls clumsy and faults for failing to develop freshman quarterback Bryce Underwood. His summary is that the talent level is down while the schedule's difficulty is up: road trips to Ohio State and Oregon, home games against Indiana, Iowa, Penn State and Oklahoma. He rates the hiring of Kyle Whittingham a substantial positive but says almost everything would have to go right for nine wins, and reads 7-5 as the likelier outcome.

*Rests on:* coaching (Moore fired, Whittingham hired); quarterback development; schedule; conference strength
